title: Netherlands pulls gold out of the US
dot:
digraph DNB_Gold_Move{graph[rankdir=TB, bgcolor="#ffffff", fontname="Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif", label=<Dutch gold leaves North America
A visual summary: from geopolitical tension to the DNB’s 86-tonne shift>, labelloc="t", pad=0.6, nodesep=0.8, ranksep=1.1];node[shape=plaintext, fontname="Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif", fontsize=11, margin=0];edge[fontname="Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif", fontsize=10, color="#666666", arrowsize=0.9, penwidth=1.1];subgraph cluster_context{label="1 · The backdrop: rising geopolitical pressure";style="rounded,filled";color="#B03A2E";fillcolor="#FDECEA";fontcolor="#B03A2E";context[label=<
● The Trump administration has shown “abrasiveness” toward traditional allies.
● Threats against Canada (“51st state”) and talk of seizing Greenland.
● Tough tariffs, NATO/EU friction and a long Russia–Ukraine war heighten unease.
>];}subgraph cluster_action{label="2 · De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) acts";style="rounded,filled";color="#D4AC0D";fillcolor="#FEF9E7";fontcolor="#7D6608";dnb[label=<
Between March and August, DNB shifted 86 tonnes of gold
Leaving North America: Federal Reserve Bank of New York & Bank of Canada (Ottawa).
Moved to: Bank of England, London — the world’s largest over-the-counter gold hub.
How: 59 tonnes sold in New York and replaced in London; 27 tonnes shipped to DNB’s Zeist vault, with a similar quantity then moved to the U.K.
The Netherlands still holds 612.4 tonnes in total (≈ €72.2 billion).
>];}subgraph cluster_rationale{label="3 · Official explanation";style="rounded,filled";color="#1E8449";fillcolor="#EAF7EF";fontcolor="#1E8449";rationale[label=<
“Gold is an anchor of trust and ideally suited to hedge extreme systemic risks.”
DNB: “We do need to strengthen our resilience and preparedness” amid “increasing geopolitical unrest.”
Bars at the Bank of England meet modern international standards, making the reserve “most readily available” in a crisis.
>];}subgraph cluster_analysis{label="4 · What analysts see behind the decision";style="rounded,filled";color="#1F618D";fillcolor="#EAF2F8";fontcolor="#1F618D";analysis[label=<
Dr Emma Shortis (Australia Institute): “A catastrophic loss of trust in the United States in Europe… gold reserves stored in the US could be used as a weapon.”
Benjamin Picton (Rabobank): “Gold is zero-counterparty asset. Europe is trying to conduct itself more independently” — the financial system’s structure is changing.
>];}subgraph cluster_pattern{label="5 · Part of a broader pattern";style="rounded,filled";color="#6C3483";fillcolor="#F4ECF7";fontcolor="#6C3483";pattern[label=<
● France: Banque de France liquidated 129 tonnes in New York in 2025, replacing them with gold stored in Paris.
● Germany: Bundesbank repatriated 674 tonnes from New York and Paris (2013–2017).
● Austria, Italy, Türkiye, Venezuela also have sought / signalled gold repatriation.
>];}context->dnb[label="drives the decision", fontcolor="#B03A2E", color="#B03A2E"];dnb->rationale[label="DNB’s stated reasons", fontcolor="#1E8449", color="#1E8449"];rationale->analysis[label="commentators respond", fontcolor="#1F618D", color="#1F618D", style=dashed];analysis->pattern[label="same pattern elsewhere", fontcolor="#6C3483", color="#6C3483", style=dotted];}
